[42037 IoT Security | Subject description]
Credit points: 6

This subject introduces you to the Internet of Things (IoT), focusing on the security challenges and solutions associated with IoT devices and networks. You'll start with an introduction to IoT security and the Contiki software environment. The subject covers a range of critical topics, including implementing IPv6 on IoT devices, authentication methods, and ReST CoAP communications, all through hands-on labs using Contiki. You will explore IoT forensic techniques, hardware security, and data security and privacy concerns, learning practical skills like security port scanning, packet crafting, and Bluetooth sniffing. The subject delves into IoT malware, smart home security, and web application vulnerabilities, providing a comprehensive view of the threats and defenses in the IoT ecosystem. Through industry-relevant projects, you will build secure IoT systems, addressing real-world security challenges and enhancing your ability to protect IoT devices and networks. The subject concludes with a review and recap of IoT security principles, ensuring you have a solid foundation to create a secure and reliable digital ecosystem.

[42037 IoT Security | Learning and teaching activities]
IoT security is designed for students to experience active and interactive learning opportunities. Students will engage in various settings including classes, labs, and workshops. They are required to complete reading and viewing materials before each class and each lab. This pre-work material will be used in classes and labs to help students to complete lab tasks to engage in discussions as well as to ask questions. Feedback will be communicated each week verbally during the completion of lab and class tasks.

[42037 IoT Security | Learning outcomes]
SLO1: Understand the current cybersecurity issues and challenges for the development security solutions in IoT networks. (B.1)
SLO2: Design IoT applications that incorporate practical security tools and technologies. (C.1)
SLO3: Develop and implement secured solutions using a simulated environment such as Contiki in a team environment. (D.1)
